title: Pay Bills: validate amount before submitting a payment
description:
Currently the One-time payment form on the Pay Bills page lets a customer submit whatever they type into the Amount field. We need basic validation before the payment is submitted so customers get clear feedback instead of a confusing result. This came out of demo feedback where a reviewer typed a letter into the amount box and the app behaved oddly.

Scope is the One-time payment form only (the Saved payees quick-pay buttons just scroll/focus that same form, so this covers both entry points).
acceptanceCriteria: Given the customer is on the Pay Bills page, when they submit the one-time payment form with a non-numeric amount (e.g. "abc"), then they should see an inline error and no payment should go through.
Given the customer enters an amount of $0 or a negative number, then they should see an inline error and no payment should go through.
Given the customer enters an amount greater than the available balance of the selected 'Pay from' account, then they should see a clear insufficient funds error and no payment should go through.
Given the customer enters a valid amount within their balance, then the payment should submit successfully as it does today.

comments.author: dev1@example.com
comments.text: Do we also need to cap the number of decimal places? E.g. someone pastes in 40.999. Not called out in the ACs, raising it here.

comments.author: qa1@example.com
comments.text: What should happen if the account balance changes between page load and submit (e.g. another payment already went through in a different tab)? Not sure if that's in scope for this ticket or a separate one.
